newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Equity trade surges after lull.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Equity trade surges after lull.

text.p: Trading in individual equity options stormed back Monday after a quiet week, with heavy trading in several issues, led by Wal-Mart Stores Inc on the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
The Wal-Mart December 22-1/2 call traded 10,920 contracts and the June 22-1/2 call traded 14,675, far outpacing volume on any other equity option.
A trader on the floor of the CBOE said an institution crossed the entire spread, selling the Junes and buying the Decembers for a customer.
"The pit crowd wasn't involved at all," he said.
Wal-Mart shares were unchanged at 25-1/2 on consolidated volume of 1.96 million shares in late trading.
On the American Stock Exchange, 9,640 Iomega Corp IOMG.O December 25 calls changed hands as the stock rallied 2-3/8 to 25 on more than six million shares.
The option traded in prices ranging from 1/2 to 1-7/16, with the options bid up later in the session.
Last Friday, fewer than 500 of those options traded, with 370 added to its open interest for a total of 19,449.
Most of Monday's trading in the option was done in relatively small blocks.
The next active Iomega option was the December 22-1/2 call, which traded more than 2,600 contracts.
Back on the CBOE, 5,000 June 10 calls on Platinum Technology Inc crossed as an institutional investor sold the position, traders said.
Platinum shares rose one to 13 after the company said it entered a global reseller agreement with Hewlett-Packard Co, which gained two to 55-7/8.
One trader at the CBOE said the news helped drive Platinum shares higher.

The busiest Hewlett option was the December 55 call, which traded more than 2,600 contracts. The January 50 put traded nearly 2,100 and the February 50 put traded 1,990, putting them atop the CBOE's most active put list.
Also in the technology sector, options on Digital Equipment Corp and America Online Inc were active as the two stocks posted sharp gains.
Digital rallied 3-3/8 to 40 after Salomon Brothers upgraded its rating to strong buy from buy.
America Online surged 4-5/8 to 39-7/8. Lehman Brothers repeated a buy rating on the stock.
Most of the action in Digital options was on the American Stock Exchange, led by the December 40 call, which traded 3,300 contracts. The January 40 call traded about 2,435.
Digital options also trade on the CBOE.
America Online options trade on the CBOE, AMEX and Pacific Stock Exchange.
Most trading Monday was done on the CBOE and Pacific Exchanges, with heavy turnover in the December 30 and 35 puts. Other busy options included the December 35 and 40 calls.
